newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen edge down on Sakakibara, seen steady.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen edge down on Sakakibara, seen steady.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures edged slightly lower on Friday after senior Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara suggested interest rates might rise.

Sakakibara, director-general of Japan's International Finance Bureau, told Reuters in an interview it would be natural for the Bank of Japan to raise rates when it had confirmed the strength of the economy.
The comments pushed the back end of SIMEX Euroyen futures down several points but the complex recovered later on as dealers decided little had changed.
Sakakibara has made similar comments before.
"Everyone is jittery about the prospect of higher rates," said one dealer. "But I don't see much immediate movement."
Dealers in Singapore said there was also some caution ahead of Japan's Golden Week holiday later in the month.
The most active December Euroyen contract hit a low of 99.02 before recovering to 99.07 at 1115 GMT, against its IMM close of 99.08. Turnover was moderate at just over 16,000 lots.
Japanese government bond (JGB) futures were knocked lower by Sakakibara's comments that the JGB market was bubbly and that there was risk of the bubble bursting.
The June SIMEX JGB contract fell briefly to a low of 126.50, down 0.30 from its open, but then recovered sharply to end at 126.85, up 0.14 on the day. Volume was a low 163 lots.
Eurodollars futures were gently firmer with December finishing at 93.490, against its IMM close at 93.485.
The market jumped on Thursday in the United States after the release of data showing U.S. exports rose four percent in February to a record $73.46 billion.
September Eurodollars ended at 93.760 against their IMM close at 93.755.
